lineage.strategy: Use achieved deployment milestones and vertical-integration evidence rather than relying on prospective commercial claims.

observations.fact: Oklo reported that its Groves low-power isotope test reactor achieved first criticality in August 2026 less than a year after groundbreaking under the DOE Reactor Pilot Program.

Oklo acquired ARMEC, adding roughly 40 engineering and manufacturing personnel plus machining, fabrication, inspection and procurement capabilities; ARMEC generated positive free cash flow in its most recent fiscal year.

risks.risk: Groves is a low-power test reactor, not proof of commercial Aurora power economics; Oklo still faces commercial licensing, fuel, financing and scale-up risk for power deployments.

unknowns.unknown: Neither source demonstrates commercial Aurora revenue, plant-level margins, delivered electricity cost or repeatable commercial construction economics.

recommendation: Credit demonstrated test-reactor execution and added manufacturing capability, but do not translate those milestones into commercial reactor economics without separate evidence.
